Photograph: Rodrique Ngowi/AP View image in fullscreen A police barricade stands outside the former home of Lindsay Clancy in Duxbury, Massachusetts, on 31 July. Photograph: Rodrique Ngowi/AP Massachusetts Jurors in Lindsay Clancy murder trial visit home where children were killed Defense lawyers say Clancy was ill with postpartum psychosis when she killed three children in January 2023 Associated Press Fri 31 Jul 2026 15.50 EDT Last modified on Fri 31 Jul 2026 18.24 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jurors walked through the Massachusetts home where Lindsay Clancy strangled her three children, a rare visit on Friday that let them see first-hand the place where an outwardly ordinary family life unraveled into tragedy . After being driven past two businesses relevant to the narrative of the January 2023 killings, jurors were escorted in groups of six to view the inside of the house, including the basement where the children died. During the roughly 40-minute visit, the jury also saw the yard where Clancy was found after jumping from a second-story window. Journalists were kept away by a police barricade, but court officers could be seen through the trees escorting jurors to and from the bus along the site of the Clancy family’s former driveway. The home now has a new owner. Lindsay Clancy’s husband told police children were dead, court hears Read more Clancy herself did not attend the visit to the home, which she has not seen since the day of the killings. Her lawyers say Clancy was in the grip of postpartum psychosis , a rare mental illness linked to the stress, sleep deprivation and hormonal changes that follow childbirth. Jurors in US criminal cases often are expressly told not to visit the scene of the events in question. There are a number of rationales for not doing so – among other things, the site may have changed in the interim between an alleged crime and a trial. But courts sometimes allow juries to make a supervised excursion as a group, for reasons that can include assessing distances or features not thought to come across fully in photos. Such excursions have happened in a number of high-profile cases, including the 2023 murder trial of the South Carolina attorney Alex Murdaugh ; the 2022 sentencing trial of Parkland, Florida, school shooter Nikolas Cruz ; the 2015 Massachusetts murder trial of former New England Patriots player Aaron Hernandez ; and the 1995 murder trial of OJ Simpson . Jurors in Clancy’s trial retraced the route her ex-husband, Patrick Clancy, took when she asked him to pick up takeout food and medicine for Cora, their five-year-old, on the night of the killings. He returned to find the children dead and Clancy badly injured and bleeding in the yard. The panel was driven past the restaurant – about 5.5 miles from the family’s former home in Duxbury, a suburb south of Boston – and the pharmacy, about a mile from the house. Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband testifies about day she killed their three children Read more Prosecutors say the errands were a ruse to get her husband out of the house. They say Lindsay Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse, acted intentionally and is criminally responsible for the deaths of children Cora, five; Dawson, three; and Callan, eight months. Her lawyers do not dispute that Clancy killed the children, but they say she had bipolar disorder and her condition worsened when she took antidepressants prescribed after the birth of her third child. Clancy believed a voice was telling her to “kill the children so you can kill yourself”, according to her lawyers. Lindsay Clancy is paralyzed from the waist down after trying to kill herself that night. Clancy faces life in prison without parole if convicted of murder. If found not guilty due to a lack of criminal responsibility, she would be committed to a state mental health facility. In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org . In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria-suspected-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5LU1l Ships often dock to load and discharge produce at refineries in oil-rich Nigeria, in thie case at the Dangote refinery in Lagos in April 2026 Image: Sodiq Adelakun/REUTERS Advertisement A Nigerian environmental NGO says that at least 37 people died in an attempt to tap oil from a loading vessel in the south of the country illegally. Most of them died as a result of inhaling hazardous fumes, the Youth and Advocacy Centre said. Nigerian authorities were yet to issue a death toll but had acknowledged a fatal incident in which people were killed, apparently while trying to steal crude oil . What do we know about the case? The incident took place overnight on Thursday in Okrika in Rivers State in the oil-rich Niger Delta in the south of the country . The environmental group said it happened at a jetty as a vessel was loading oil from the Indorama Eleme Petrochemical through the Port Harcourt Refinery. The people who died were "suspected oil thieves" trying to siphon the commodity off into boats at an "illegal tapping point." The Youth and Advocacy Centre NGO said that other people were still missing, potentially lost in the water, quoting a network of volunteers. Police acknowledged an incident but said they continued to investigate the details. "The Rivers State Police Command can confirm the deaths. The victims were allegedly attempting to steal crude oil," said spokesperson Blessing Agbabe. Africa's fuel crisis: Is Dangote the answer? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Oil theft is fairly common in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, Africa's biggest oil producer , with oil mining areas hotspots for poverty and environmental degradation. The Nigerian government estimates that oil theft causes losses worth several billion dollars annually and has been trying to clamp down on the practice. The tapping process can also cause leaks and environmental damage. If confirmed this would be the worst fatal accident on record connected to attempted oil theft since at least October 2023. However the Nigeria Security and Civil Defense Corps said that the casualty figures circulating remained unverified, saying it was working with other security agencies to clarify the details. https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.text: Bookmakers, slot machine venues and casinos won £12.6bn from customers in Britain last year, with official figures suggesting up to 1.4 million people have a gambling problem. Photograph: David Colbran/Alamy View image in fullscreen Bookmakers, slot machine venues and casinos won £12.6bn from customers in Britain last year, with official figures suggesting up to 1.4 million people have a gambling problem. Photograph: David Colbran/Alamy Gambling Peers call for UK to enact tobacco-style ban on gambling advertising Lords’ report faces criticism from lobby groups after suggesting ban would be ‘most effective’ way to reduce public harms Rob Davies Thu 17 Sep 2026 02.00 EDT Last modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 06.06 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The UK should introduce a ban on almost all gambling advertising to protect public health, a cross-party group of peers has urged, prompting fury from the lobby group for bookmakers and casinos. In a 173-page report, the House of Lords liaison committee said the government had been “too passive” in response to an explosion of digital advertising and social media influencers promoting the gambling sector. British bookmakers, slot machine venues and casinos won £12.6bn from customers in Great Britain last year, while up to 1.4 million people have a gambling problem , according to official statistics. Online bookies accused of UK privacy breaches with use of cookie banners Read more The report found that a tobacco-style blanket ban on advertising, with carve-outs for the lottery and racecourses, would be the “most effective” way to reduce harms such as financial ruin, relationship breakdown and even suicide. A ban would likely result in the UK’s gambling sector shrinking, the report acknowledged, but would lead to longer-term economic benefit as money previously spent on gambling is diverted to other parts of the economy. The report was dismissed as “deeply misguided” by the industry’s lobby group, the Betting & Gaming Council (BGC), which said any such policy could increase harm because it would benefit the illicit market, which would continue to advertise. Lord Foster, one of the report’s authors, said the illicit market, whose exploitative activities have been documented in Guardian investigations , was a “legitimate concern” and pointed to ongoing efforts by regulators to crack down on rogue sites. “That should not deflect us from the need to address the harm that is being created by the legal market,” he said, insisting there was a wealth of evidence linking gambling advertising to harm. Gambling advertising in the UK was liberalised via the 2005 Gambling Act introduced by Tony Blair’s government, a landmark piece of legislation that aimed to regulate the sector but also promote its growth as a legitimate leisure activity that could create jobs and boost the economy. Before the act, only bingo, the football pools and lotteries, including the National Lottery, were allowed to advertise on television. The volume of gambling advertising has ballooned since then, with annual spend by the industry reaching £2bn in 2024, according to estimates . In contrast to Blair, Andy Burnham has been a vocal critic of the gambling industry and recently moved to give councils more power to block new betting shops and “slot farms” opening up on high streets. As mayor of Greater Manchester, he expressed a desire to “relegate gambling sponsorship of sport to the history books”. The BGC pointed to voluntary measures already taken by the industry, including “whistle to whistle” ban that saw its members agree not to advertise during the course of a televised sports fixture. The trade body has also estimated that half of the money spent on advertising by gambling firms now comes from a fast-growing illicit market not subject to the same controls as licensed operators. Grainne Hurst, the BGC chief executive, said:“A blanket advertising ban would remove a key competitive advantage of being licensed and regulated while doing nothing to stop illegal operators targeting British consumers.” The Guardian ceased accepting advertising from gambling companies , excluding the National Lottery, in 2024. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/09/flyd.text: The co-pilot who attacked the captain of a flydubai jet on 30 September had planned to crash the aircraft into Tel Aviv's international airport, according to the United Arab Emirates' top prosecutor.The Omani co-pilot was inspired by Al-Qaeda's September 11, 2001 attacks on the United States and intended to cause "the greatest possible loss of life", according to the prosecutor's findings published by state media."The findings showed that he had met the professional and security requirements for employment, including holding a pilot's licence, providing a certificate of good conduct and completing the required checks."Passengers described storming the cockpit and struggling to regain control after the aircraft suddenly dropped around 5,000 metres.The plane's Indian captain was injured when the co-pilot attacked him with an axe, but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to subdue the attacker. The aircraft then made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.Most passengers on board were Israeli.On Thursday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog awarded the Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism to six Israelis who helped foil the recent attempted flydubai hijacking.“The civilian bravery and resourcefulness demonstrated by the heroes present here cannot overshadow the obligation to obtain full answers. Everyone, all of us, deserves clear and satisfactory answers,” he said as reported by The Jerusalem Post.Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised the passengers and the pilot for their bravery in thwarting the attack and ordered a "thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel".
